findings.text: The routine kvm_arch_guest_memory_reclaimed is a file external hook that forwards a guest memory reclaim notification for a given VM to the vendor specific reclaim handler. The shown fragment performs direct delegation with no extra filtering or state updates.

The predicate kvm_dirty_ring_check_request decides whether vCPU entry must abort for dirty ring pressure. When the soft full request is present and the ring still reports soft full, it reasserts the request, records a dirty ring full exit reason, emits the dirty ring exit trace event and returns true to force an exit to userspace. Otherwise it returns false and allows entry to continue.

The routine vcpu_enter_guest is the central driver for preparing, entering and leaving guest execution on x86. It drains pending control requests, handles event injection and MMU reload, switches host state for guest entry, loops over the vendor run handler while reentry is requested, then restores host state, accounts time and statistics and delegates final exit processing to the vendor exit handler.

The helper vcpu_block implements the sleep and wake path for a vCPU that is not runnable. It temporarily switches from hypervisor timer to software timer, releases SRCU protection across halt or generic block, restores timer mode on wake, evaluates nested and APIC events before leaving halt, and advances halted or reset hold states to runnable while leaving init received state unchanged.

Pending exceptions dominate other injectable work in the event path. Fault class vectors cause the resume flag identified by X86_EFLAGS_RF to be set in the flags image managed through the rflags helpers before injection, while trap like cases and debug vectors preserve the existing flag value. A debug vector identified by DB_VECTOR with general detect set in debug control identified by DR7_GD first clears that detect bit and refreshes the hardware debug control. Injection then clears the pending marker, sets the injected marker and disables further injection for the current pass.

After exception handling, guest debug blocking of interrupts is honored by returning early without injecting interrupt class events. When system management support is compiled in, system management interrupts are considered first, followed by nonmaskable interrupts and regular interrupts. Each class is injectable only when no reinjection is required and the vendor allowed check succeeds. A busy indication requests an immediate exit and preserves the event request. An allowed but architecturally blocked event arms the corresponding vendor window. Nested mode with pending nested events also forces an immediate exit.

Queueing a fresh exception while an event is being injected risks an infinite cycle of aborted entries followed by re injection. The code therefore warns if either the main pending marker or the VM exit pending marker remains set at the end of event processing. Triple faults are exempted because they use special handling that does not repeat the cycle, including real mode event emulation without unrestricted guest support.

The APIC virtualization refresh is a no operation without an in kernel local APIC. When the vCPU runs in x2APIC mode on hardware that permits APIC virtualization in that mode without full x2APIC virtualization, the logic inhibits the APIC access page to avoid incorrect MMIO access to the virtual APIC page through stale mappings. The inhibition is sticky for simplicity. The vendor specific refresh then runs unconditionally after that guard.

The IOAPIC scan refreshes the set of vectors handled through the IOAPIC path. It exits early without a present APIC, otherwise clears a 256 entry handled vector bitmap, resets the highest stale pending end of interrupt marker to negative one, synchronizes the posted interrupt vector to the in service state, collects routes from the split irqchip scanner or the in kernel IOAPIC scanner, and either defers the end of interrupt map load for nested guests or raises a load request for normal guests.

Loading of the end of interrupt exit map is skipped unless the local APIC hardware is enabled. For HyperV associated vCPUs the logic merges the IOAPIC handled vectors with the SynIC vector bitmap into a 256 bit map and passes that merged map to the vendor loader. For other vCPUs it passes the IOAPIC handled vectors directly to the vendor loader.

Reload of the APIC access page address is conditional on the presence of an in kernel local APIC. When present it delegates to the vendor setter for the access page address. There is no additional state change in the shown fragment.

Entry preparation implements a request draining state machine where each pending control request is tested and cleared once per pass. Recognized requests cover VM liveness, dirty ring pressure, nested state pages, obsolete MMU roots, timer migration, master and global and per vCPU clocks, MMU sync and page directory load, full and local TLB flushes, TPR access reporting, triple fault, async page fault halt, steal time, performance monitor events and interrupts, nonmaskable processing, IOAPIC end of interrupt and scan and map load, APIC page reload, APIC virtualization update, async fault completion, intercept recalculation, dirty logging update, protected guest state, and virtual machine save area reload. System management, HyperV TLB flush and HyperV crash reset exit and timer requests appear only when the corresponding support is compiled in. Several requests terminate the pass with a userspace exit reason or a return to the outer run loop.

TLB maintenance observes a defined order. The full flush request is serviced before local flush requests because a full flush also satisfies pending local flushes. HyperV precise per vCPU flush is attempted when requested and on failure falls back to a full guest flush. Although initiated per vCPU, HyperV flushes are treated as remote because they can be requested from other vCPUs. HyperV SynIC timers are processed after clock update because they depend on fresh guest time.

The event injection path inside guest entry triggers when the event request is present or an interrupt window is wanted with an accepted direct interrupt or a Xen interrupt is pending. It counts the event attempt, accepts local APIC events with failure treated as a userspace exit, pauses init received vCPUs in the outer loop, invokes the shared check and inject routine, arms the interrupt window when a window was requested, and refreshes CR8 interception and virtual APIC synchronization when the local APIC is enabled.

Guest entry uses a layered exclusion protocol. Preemption is disabled and the vendor prepare handler runs, then local interrupts are disabled before publishing guest mode. The mode transition to guest uses release ordering, followed by SRCU unlock and a barrier that orders the mode store against request checks, posted interrupt state and page table reads. Pending posted interrupts are synchronized regardless of APIC virtualization state because assigned devices can post even while virtualization is inhibited. If an exit is already requested, mode reverts to outside guest with a write barrier before re enabling interrupts and preemption and reacquiring SRCU.

Immediately before guest entry the code stabilizes extended CPU state. It asserts FPU consistency, loads FPU state when needed, restores the extended feature error reporting register when the guest has a pending error, loads guest extended features, programs guest debug registers from the effective values with special handling for the no exit and auto switch modes, refreshes the host debug control snapshot after interrupts are disabled and flags vendor reload when host owned bits changed and guest state is not protected, loads mediated performance state, enters guest time accounting with interrupts off and swaps protection key state while hardware breakpoints are quiescent.

The low level run loop invokes the vendor run handler until the result differs from reenter guest. Each reentry synchronizes posted interrupts, aborts to a handled exit when an exit is requested, clears one shot flags and counts the exit. After the loop the code restores protection keys and performance state, synchronizes debug registers when no exit debug mode was used, restores host breakpoints, records last CPU and timestamp, publishes outside guest mode, restores host extended features, synchronizes disable state when needed, runs the vendor irq off handler, clears the error register, marks branch predictor flush when required, consumes pending interrupts with accounting, exits guest timing, re enables interrupts and preemption, reacquires SRCU, profiles the exit address when enabled, re arms clock update for catchup mode, syncs virtual APIC attention and calls the vendor exit handler.

Two early failure paths share a cancellation protocol. MMU reload failure and an exit request observed after publishing guest mode both abandon entry, preserve an immediate exit event request when one was armed, invoke the vendor cancellation handler to drop a partially injected event and synchronize virtual APIC state when attention is pending. Omitting cancellation would leave a half injected event visible to the next entry attempt.

Guest time accounting around entry and exit is bracketed by instrumentation guards. Entry assumes ioctl context and attributes pending time to the guest, while exit flushes guest time back to host accounting. Both helpers run with interrupts disabled and perform no other state changes in the shown fragments.

Dirty ring pressure implements a non runnable gate. While the soft full request is set and the ring reports soft full, the vCPU is forced to exit with a dirty ring full reason instead of entering the guest. The request remains asserted until userspace harvests entries and resets the ring, preventing further guest execution in the meantime.

Multiprocessor state advances only after sleep and event acceptance succeed. Halted and reset hold states move to runnable on wake, runnable remains runnable, and init received remains parked without clearing halted async fault state. Runnable entry clears the async fault halted marker. Any unrecognized state triggers a one time warning. A negative nested event check other than busy, or a failed APIC acceptance, aborts the transition and returns to the caller without changing state.

Blocking releases SRCU protection across the sleep to avoid holding read side critical sections while descheduled, then reacquires it before touching vCPU state again. Hypervisor timer mode is swapped to software before halt polling or blocking so that an expired guest timer is observed as a wake event, and restored to hypervisor mode after wake when it was previously in use. Signals that leave the vCPU non runnable return to the caller without altering activity state.

Event and virtualization state is spread across per vCPU fields observed here. Exception state carries pending and injected markers plus vector. Reinjection need gates new injection. System management state carries pending and count. Nonmaskable state carries pending and injected markers. Interrupt handling uses injectable checks, queued vectors and window arming. IOAPIC handling uses a 256 entry bitmap, a pending vector index and a stale marker plus a deferred load flag or explicit load request. APIC virtualization uses active and activated markers, access page inhibition and attention flags. Entry bookkeeping uses mode, host debug control, extended feature error, debug register selection with effective values, last CPU and timestamp, and performance mediation state.

Userspace exit payloads share a common run structure with a reason discriminator and per reason details. Observed reasons include internal error with emulation suberror, TPR access, shutdown with cleared MMIO need, IOAPIC end of interrupt with vector, system events for crash and reset, HyperV exit with copied vendor payload, and dirty ring full. Clock, steal, performance and timer requests update in kernel state without producing an exit in the shown paths.

The control interface uses stable symbolic discriminators. Exit reasons observed include KVM_EXIT_INTERNAL_ERROR with KVM_INTERNAL_ERROR_EMULATION and KVM_EXIT_TPR_ACCESS and KVM_EXIT_SHUTDOWN and KVM_EXIT_IOAPIC_EOI and KVM_EXIT_SYSTEM_EVENT with KVM_SYSTEM_EVENT_CRASH and KVM_SYSTEM_EVENT_RESET and KVM_EXIT_HYPERV and KVM_EXIT_DIRTY_RING_FULL. Request identifiers observed include KVM_REQ_EVENT and KVM_REQ_VM_DEAD and KVM_REQ_DIRTY_RING_SOFT_FULL and KVM_REQ_GET_NESTED_STATE_PAGES and KVM_REQ_MMU_FREE_OBSOLETE_ROOTS and KVM_REQ_CLOCK_UPDATE with related master and global variants and KVM_REQ_TLB_FLUSH with local variants and KVM_REQ_TRIPLE_FAULT and KVM_REQ_APF_HALT and KVM_REQ_NMI with related SMI variant and KVM_REQ_IOAPIC_EOI_EXIT and KVM_REQ_SCAN_IOAPIC and KVM_REQ_LOAD_EOI_EXITMAP and KVM_REQ_APICV_UPDATE among others for timers performance intercepts logging protected state and save area.

Multiprocessor control uses KVM_MP_STATE_RUNNABLE and KVM_MP_STATE_HALTED and KVM_MP_STATE_INIT_RECEIVED and KVM_MP_STATE_AP_RESET_HOLD. Guest debug control uses KVM_GUESTDBG_BLOCKIRQ to suppress interrupt injection. Debug and flag facilities use DB_VECTOR and DR7_GD and X86_EFLAGS_RF and DR7_FIXED_1 with related register numbers. Vendor run control uses KVM_RUN_FORCE_IMMEDIATE_EXIT and KVM_RUN_LOAD_GUEST_DR6 and KVM_RUN_LOAD_DEBUGCTL. Guest mode uses IN_GUEST_MODE and OUTSIDE_GUEST_MODE. Profiling uses KVM_PROFILING.

The IOAPIC end of interrupt path enforces a vector bound. A pending vector beyond the valid range triggers a fatal check, while a vector outside the handled set is silently ignored instead of exiting. Virtual APIC attention observed after entry preparation, after cancellation and after exit causes a synchronization from the virtual APIC, so missing that synchronization would leave stale interrupt state.

Per vCPU and per VM APIC virtualization state must remain consistent across updates. The entry loop warns when the activated marker disagrees with the active marker unless the APIC is disabled, relying on kicks and waits to serialize updates with request handling. Profiling of exit addresses is restricted to the profiling mode with unprotected guest state. Extended feature disable synchronization is required before the irq off exit handler when write interception is disabled.
